catalog_quote: Apart from these features, Katuic languages are phonologically typical Austroasiatic languages of the lower Mekong region with prosodic words of a maximally disyllabic, iambic template and vowel inventories with nine to eleven vowel qualities (Gehrmann and Conver 2015, Jenny et al. 2015). ... PK words may be monosyllables or disyllables. The final syllable or main syllable of a disyllabic word is always prosodically prominent and phonotactically unrestricted while the penultimate syllable or presyllable is always unstressed and phonotactically restricted with respect to the main syllable. A monosyllable is by definition a main syllable without a presyllable and, therefore, phonotactically equivalent to the main syllable of a disyllabic word. ... The PK phonological word is a maximally disyllabic iamb (cf. Butler 2015a) but not a sesquisyllable in the original sense of the word as coined by Matisoff (1973). ... The description of the PK word above does not accurately describe the prosodic word of any one modern Katuic language. Various phonological changes both big and small have affected the presyllable structure of the modern Katuic languages. ... Robust Presyllables Pacoh, E. Bru, N. Katang, W. Katu ... Transitional /ʔN.C/ [ʔN̩.C] Pacoh [pac], E. Bru [bru], N. Katang [ncq]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are maximally disyllabic iambs: stress (prosodic prominence) falls on the final (main) syllable; a preceding presyllable/minor syllable, if present, is always unstressed and phonologically reduced. Northern Katang is classed among the Katuic languages with 'robust presyllables' (contrastive /a/ vs /u/ in open presyllables after velars, contrastive sesquisyllabicity), but these presyllables remain unstressed with no length or register contrast (Gehrmann 2016: 76-77).
new_statements.exceptions: None; monosyllables are by definition main syllables. Compounds/longer loans not discussed for N. Katang.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological/prosodic word (native lexicon, citation forms from wordlist elicitation); statement is framed for Proto-Katuic and the modern Katuic languages generally, with N. Katang [ncq] explicitly included in the paper's typology tables; author's N. Katang data are first-hand (one speaker, Phin district).
new_statements.identity_note: Northern Katang [ncq]/nort3270 was created by ISO 639-3 CR 2016-021 (split of [kgd]); the request forms (Cheeseman & Gehrmann) identify it with the 'Katang Phin' (KatP) variety of Gehrmann 2016 and Gehrmann & Conver 2015: one speaker from Phin district, Savannakhet province, north of the Salavan/Savannakhet border range. Gehrmann 2018 labels the same variety 'N. Katang [ncq]'. The stress statement quoted is a Katuic-family-level statement (Proto-Katuic word template said to be continued by the modern languages) in a paper that names N. Katang [ncq] explicitly and whose author collected the N. Katang data first-hand; it is not a dedicated phonology of Northern Katang (none exists in Glottolog, the Payap thesis list, or the sources' bibliographies). Not to be confused with Southern Katang [sct] (Katang Rueal, Huffman's 1979 Katang; sout3251) or 'Katang Ta'oiq' (Ferlus's Katang = Upper Ta'oih [tth]).
